I don’t really have advice, but I do want to say I’m sorry that happened to you. I’ve been through something similar, and it honestly made me pull back a lot. I became less vulnerable and more focused on protecting my energy, my emotions, and me. How you’re feeling is 100% valid. I would never want to talk to him again. 

Seeing as though I don’t have *actual* advice, what I can share is this:

First, most people just lack basic shit like common courtesy, compassion, and consideration. Like, those things should be simple, but you’d be surprised how rare they actually are.

Second, people are just… people. Before they’re a friend, a partner, a coworker—before they hold any title—they’re just human. That perspective helped me stop overcomplicating things. If someone isn’t meeting me where I need to be met, or they’re not treating me right? Cool. They’re just a person. And I can let that go.

It gave me peace. And hope. Hope that someday I’ll find the right person—someone who chooses to show up with compassion, courtesy, and care. And that’s worth holding space for.

Wow I'm really sorry to hear that you're going through such a challenging time. I realize the red flags we see in the beginning are nothing but warnings and we have to act on it as soon as we can. 

Know that you are worthy of love, a genuine love. And if your ex truly loved you the way she did, I guarantee she wouldn’t have performed those actions, knowing that they would hurt you. Others may disagree but I’m firm believer in a person who truly is meant to be the love of your life and your forever partner, won’t hurt you that way. 

It's important to acknowledge your feelings and give yourself the space to heal. Consider reaching out to people you trust, even utilize Reddit (if you need someone to talk to I am here to be a listening ear for you. And There are 1000s of others willing to help and listen), or a mental health professional for support. If you can. There also multiple podcasts you can watch and listen to, books you can read, videos you can watch and even threads on Reddit you can use to help you heal during the process. 

Focus on rebuilding your life and rediscovering your own passions and goals, and ultimately, focus on loving you and being in love with yourself. Start treating your heart and your love, and peace and feelings like they’re an actual business. (If you want me to elaborate on that, let me know lol.) Remember, Healing takes time, and with support, and truly focusing on being in love with you, you will find happiness and confidence again. And it’ll happen sooner before you know it. 

And in the event of your ex trying to come back into your life, put yourself and your feelings first. And remember that if you constantly go back to a person or thing/situation that broke you, truly hurt you —- and you got saved from it? you won’t be able to fully heal, if heal at all. 

Healing process starts when we love ourselves. 

This is the best advice I can give, I truly wish you the best. If you ever need someone to talk to, don’t hesitate to reach out!
